Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. books/kestrel/rust/syntax/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp contains pipe-escaped symbol names for Rust lexical-grammar terminals (e.g. |CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|, |CST-";"-LEAFTERM|) whose embedded quote and semicolon characters a naive grep flags, but a check for true comment lines (^;) returns 0, confirming the same bare-symbol/tuple format as every other file in this rule, matching the pattern already established for a Java grammar file in an earlier unit.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 54 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, confirming bare-symbol/tuple format with no declaration content.

grep -c for '"' and ';' returned 0 for 53 of the 54 files; books/kestrel/rust/syntax/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp returned 62 and 1 respectively, traced line-by-line to pipe-escaped grammar-terminal symbol names, with grep -n '^;' confirming zero true comment lines.

evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. books/kestrel/rust/syntax/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp contains pipe-escaped symbol names for Rust lexical-grammar terminals (e.g. |CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|, |CST-";"-LEAFTERM|) whose embedded quote and semicolon characters a naive grep flags, but a check for true comment lines (^;) returns 0, confirming the same bare-symbol/tuple format as every other file in this rule, matching the pattern already established for a Java grammar file in an earlier unit.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 54 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, confirming bare-symbol/tuple format with no declaration content.

grep -c for '"' and ';' returned 0 for 53 of the 54 files; books/kestrel/rust/syntax/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp returned 62 and 1 respectively, traced line-by-line to pipe-escaped grammar-terminal symbol names, with grep -n '^;' confirming zero true comment lines.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.

justification: Byte-identical formal-source documents contain the same searchable file body, but their source and module paths are independent provenance and search signals. All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.
title: Exact-content duplicate formal source
